subject: System Design
title: Polyglot Persistence
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Polyglot Persistence.

hook.text: Netflix uses Cassandra for user data, Elasticsearch for search, and Redis for sessions. Three databases, one app.

buildup.text: Polyglot persistence means using different databases for different parts of the same application.

discovery.text: Each database excels at its specific workload: caching, search, relationships, or time-series data.

twist.text: More databases means more operational complexity: backups, monitoring, failover, and expertise for each.

climax.text: Polyglot persistence gives the best performance but the highest complexity. Start simple, specialize as needed.

punchline.text: Use the best database for each job, not one for all.

quiz.question: What is polyglot persistence?
options: Using different databases for different parts of an application
